Focusing (Eugene Gendlin's method of listening to a vague, felt sense in your body) can especially help you notice feelings and preferences the part you've been playing learned to overlook. Any words you put to them can stay tentative ("I hate cooking... or just for everybody?") while you look at what they seem to mean and revise how you read them. Some people also benefit from temporary, intentional distance from whoever they've been playing the part for, long enough for conditioning to quiet down and real preferences to surface.

guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
Untangling the Belonging Bargains

Identity formation also requires untangling from family emotional systems, religious orthodoxies, group identities, political tribes, and individual relationships that pull you away from your own knowing in exchange for belonging.

Most social systems ask for some conformity. Families want a particular kind of son, daughter, or sibling. Religions want particular beliefs and behavior. Political tribes expect consistent positions and predictable reactions. Friend groups develop rules about acceptable topics, humor, and emotion. A relationship can require one performance of self to keep the bond intact.

brief:
- building who you are also means untangling yourself from whatever pulls you away from your own knowing in exchange for belonging. The article already has the controlling family, the strict church, and the relationship you keep up a fake version of yourself for. What's new here: the pull also comes from group identities and political tribes, and from ordinary families and religions, not only harsh ones
- most social systems ask for some conformity, and that much is ordinary (keep "some": the bargain is giving yourself up, not every compromise). Families want a particular kind of son, daughter or sibling; religions want particular beliefs and behavior; political tribes expect consistent positions and predictable reactions; friend groups develop rules about what you can talk about, joke about and feel. The guide gives these one sentence each, which marches; the writer decides the form
- context, not for the text: Also Look Outward already has the relationship that needs "a fake normal, happy version of yourself to hold onto it", so don't repeat it
- context, not for the text: untangling isn't leaving, and it isn't against family or faith as such (the stance ledger). The next paragraph says what a belonging bargain is (earning worth in an arena), so this one doesn't have to define it
